What started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

The Mole (2001 – 2008, 2022 – 2024)

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

The Mole (2001 – 2008, 2022 – 2024)
at Netflix
at Netflix

The Devil's Plan (2023 – )

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Plan on Netflix.

The Devil's Plan (2023 – )
at Netflix
at Netflix

The Circle (2020 – )

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole new persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

The Circle (2020 – )
at Hulu
at Hulu

Million Dollar Secret (2025 – )

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

Million Dollar Secret (2025 – )
at Netflix
at Netflix

House of Villains (2023 – )

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

House of Villains (2023 – )
at Peacock
at Peacock

The 8 Show (2024)

This is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

The 8 Show (2024)
at Netflix
at Netflix

The Trust: A Game of Greed (2024)

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

The Trust: A Game Of Greed (2024)
at Netflix
at Netflix

Outlast (2023 – )

Blending the Big Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

Outlast (2023 – )
at Netflix
at Netflix

007: Road to a Million (2023 – )

The tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

007: Road to a Million (2023 – )
at Prime Video
at Prime Video

Squid Game (2021 – 2025)

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

title: Corporate Leaders Discuss the Future of India’s Economy at TIME Impact Dinner
content:
Corporate leaders in India spoke about the country’s economic growth and potential in the coming years at TIME’s The Partnership Imperative: Building the Next Chapter of Growth dinner in Andhra Pradesh on Thursday. 

Speaking on the panel were Madhur Jain, co- founder and CEO of Varaha ClimateAg, a climate tech start-up; Anupriya Acharya, CEO in South Asia of Publicis Groupe, an international marketing and public relations firm; Rajesh Mittal, president of the automotive company Isuzu Motors India; and Mio Oka, the director of India operations at Asian Development Bank.

Acharya spoke about the importance of flexibility when creating business opportunities across India’s vast network of markets and regions. 

“Flexibility starts from a point where you are not treating everything the same, and it's not like you can do copy-paste on the same solution from one market to the other,” she said. “It doesn't work like that.” In order to tend to the needs of multiple businesses, she said, “you have to solve for each of the sectors, each of the clients, each of the segments … starting from their own context.”

Acharya also discussed the ways in which AI can provide quantitative insights into the economy and how to leverage that data. 

“The amount of data that is available is absolutely mind-blowing and mind-boggling,” she said, while stressing that for a business to thrive, it needs a qualitative understanding of the country as well as data-driven insights. “You need the qualitative aspects, the understanding of culture, understanding of India, the understanding of consumers, markets to decode … how you could plan for the future.”

Oka talked about the ways in which India can continue to improve in some key business areas. 

“So, what's missing in India? Two things. One is manufacturing lead growth. Second is technology,” she said. She added that the agriculture business is another key component to India’s economy that should increasingly be invested in. 

She also said that there must be “real dialogue" between the government and companies to address systemic issues in the country.

“We know there are issues about labor. We know there are issues about land. So why don't we talk about it?” she asked. “It's a good time that we start tackling the fundamental problems that we have, and this is why the transparent, honest dialog based on trust, is very important.”

Jain also discussed the importance of India’s agriculture industry. 

“India has 162 million hectares of crop land area. India always had incredible talent, which is now matched with a lot of ambition and capital as well,” he said. “It's important that there is an eye upon these upcoming areas which can fetch billions of dollars and bring them into the country.”

Mittal said that India’s export economy should become the country’s focus, if it wants to see continued growth in the years to come.

“We have to become export oriented, and that can come only when we start thinking on building trust through quality, through discipline, through systems, through processes,” he said. “We have a lot of manpower, so we have a lot of potential to become a manufacturing hub.”

The Partnership Imperative: Building the Next Chapter of Growth was presented by Andhra Pradesh.

title: Brooklyn Apartment Building Collapses, Killing 8: What To Know
content:
Eight people, two of whom were children, died after an apartment building in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed on Wednesday.

The building, located at 1321 Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn’s Flatbush neighborhood, collapsed “into an adjacent construction site,” the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said in a statement on social media. Eighteen people were wounded in the incident, including one person who is in critical condition, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a press conference on Thursday.

Here’s what we know about the situation.

What happened?

The cause of the building collapse is under investigation, city officials have said.

FDNY said that crews responded to the site of the incident around 4 p.m. on Wednesday and began a search-and-rescue operation. More than 250 first responders were at the site of the collapse.

City officials reported Wednesday evening that two people had died. That number rose to eight by Thursday morning as rescue operations continued.

Mamdani said at the Thursday press conference that six of the eight people who died in the building collapse were adults and two were children. Six of the deceased died at the scene and two at nearby hospitals. Two of the people who died were construction workers at the adjacent site, located at 2625 Bedford Avenue, Mamdani said.

The mayor said that at least 18 other people were injured—four of them firefighters, and the other 14 civilians. Mamdani said that “the vast majority” of the people who are being treated in hospitals for their injuries are in stable condition, while one individual is in critical condition. 

Mamdani said on Thursday that the tragedy has been “devastating” for the city.

“I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost,” the mayor said. “These were our friends and our neighbors, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad, and beyond. Let us continue to hold close those who have been plunged into unimaginable grief, and pray for a full and rapid recovery for every New Yorker injured.”

The city has not released the identities of the eight people who died. The Ecuadorian consul, though, said in a social media post on Thursday that two of the victims had been identified and were Ecuadorian: Gabriel Ariolfo Siguencia Yupa and José Luis Caguana Cosquillo.

What is the status of rescue operations?

Rescue operations continued into Thursday. FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said at the press conference that day that the heavy rain hitting the city on Thursday “will not stop our operations here,” adding, though, that the inclement weather “will definitely hinder our efforts.” A few hours later, shortly after 4 p.m., the FDNY announced on social media that it had “concluded rescue operations throughout the entire site and determined there are no more victims.”

Bonsignore previously explained to the public that operations for a building collapse such as this one “are extremely dangerous.”

“Multiple people from the building and the construction site were trapped,” Bonsignore said in a statement on Wednesday, predicting that “this will be a prolonged operation.”

What is the city doing in response to the building collapse?

Mamdani said on Thursday that anyone who has not been able to get into contact with someone who they think could have been affected by the incident should call 311—or 212-639-9675, if they are located outside of the city.

The city has also opened a center to help people who were affected or displaced by the collapse; the center is located at the Flatbush YMCA at 1401 Flatbush Avenue.

The mayor said on Thursday that there are “five main entities involved” with the construction site adjacent to the collapsed building that are also connected to about 100 other sites across New York City, and that the NYC Department of Buildings “is commencing sweeps of those sites to ensure that if there is anything New Yorkers need to be worried about, that we are on the scene and we are doing something about it.”

Mamdani also emphasized that “a tragedy of this magnitude demands a comprehensive and thorough investigation that includes both the construction site and the building which collapsed.” He said that the city has already started its investigation, which is being led by the NYC Department of Buildings and law enforcement officials.

“We will find out what happened, and we will share that information with New Yorkers,” he said. “I will just underline: If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable."

title: Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good
content:
Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon and Best Buy, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Nintendo's Black Friday deals

On Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console. Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.99, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games. During this promotion, each of the following is $39.99:

  • Donkey Kong Bananza

  • Kirby Air Riders

  • Metroid Prime 4: Beyond

  • Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

  • Super Mario Party: Jamboree

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. Games like Donkey Kong Bananza retail for upwards of $69.99, so you're saving as much as $30 on these games during this week-long promotion. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale.

Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in New York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

Back Friday 2026 FAQs

Are Black Friday deals worth it?

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything. 

How do I make the most of Black Friday? 

Use price tracking tools to determine if the deals you're keeping tabs on are actually a deal. If you feel like that's too much work, we already do that for you, so follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products makes you focus and make smarter decisions.

title: Trump Wants Apple's Tim Cook to Replace Jensen Huang as NVIDIA CEO
content:
President Trump suggested on Thursday that Tim Cook, former CEO of Apple, should become the leader of chip maker Nvidia following its chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over his alleged affairs with two women. 

“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! ” Trump posted on TruthSocial. 

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday morning, in the wake of reports that he had allegedly been involved in two affairs, including one with a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy.

It is unclear if Trump has reached out to Cook regarding this suggestion. TIME has reached out to the White House for comment. 

Huang and the White House have maintained a close relationship since the start of Trump’s second term. During his official visit to China in May, Trump invited Huang to attend the summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The New York Times reported that the President insisted on inviting Huang to join the delegation despite concerns over Huang’s relationship with a woman who is believed to be a Chinese spy. 

Speaking with reporters on Monday, Trump repeatedly downplayed Huang’s alleged affair, insisting that he believed the tech billionaire’s assertion that he knew nothing about the alleged espionage operation.

“I really believe him,” Trump told reporters during the White House press conference. “I think that he’ll be in good shape.”

title: The Toxic Vengeance of Capital Punishment
content:
Two radical ideas have been introduced into human thought, wrote the novelist and humorist Kurt Vonnegut. One was that “energy and matter are pretty much the same sort of stuff.” That was Einstein. The other was that “revenge is a bad idea.” That was Jesus. We are so wired for vengeance, so trained to retaliate, mused Vonnegut, Jesus must be classed among the revolutionaries. 

Vonnegut was no Christian, preferring to describe himself as a “Christ-worshipping agnostic,” but he dreamed of a world in which the long “chain of death and destruction” is broken. That is why he opposed the death penalty and one of the reasons he despaired of America.

News that the execution of former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan, who murdered 13 U.S. soldiers in 2009, will not be livestreamed in December has been well received, but reports that a narrow majority of Americans approve of both the sentence and the method of death-by-firing-squad have excited little comment.

Coming days after the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee, for a crime committed when she was a teenager, it is reasonable to ask: Why do we still execute people?

Pope Leo has protested the cruelty of a practice that denies “the possibility of redemption,” but this is a political as well as a religious question. A culture of vengeance tears at the fabric of democracy.

About 20 years ago, the legal scholar Terry Aladjem staged a debate on the death penalty for an undergraduate class at the University of Massachusetts in Boston. Expecting to have to work hard to convince students of its merits, Aladjem was shocked to discover that nearly all of them were in favor of capital punishment. The “class erupted,” he recalled. “Those who supported the death penalty vastly outnumbered their opponents. America was not what I thought it was.” 

Aladjem went on to write a book about vengeance and how our appetite for violent punishment throws us back into a state of nature, fanning the dangerous passions that are supposed to be cooled and contained by the social contract.

Vengeance was becoming the air we breathe, he observed. Talk shows, television justice, and politics seemed to be concerned with little else. Where liberal thought had banished the criterion of revenge from all considerations of justice, a politics of purity had brought it back. The result was “something absolutist, something profoundly undemocratic,” wrote Aladjem. The president who wants to hunt down terrorists, “dead or alive,” and the angry talk show host “who entertains the views of others only to reinforce his own” were peas in a pod. For Aladjem, the death penalty is at once deeply problematic on its own and a symptom of a wider malaise. He fears that the glee we might feel in the death of a “bad person” will come for us in the end.

J. William Fulbright, the Senator for Arkansas and a longtime critic of the Vietnam War, made the same point in an essay on “The American Character” after the assassination of John F. Kennedy. Fulbright was appalled by the widespread expressions of sympathy for Jack Ruby, the man who shot Kennedy’s alleged assassin live on television, thus depriving Lee Harvey Oswald of one of the basic rights of a civilized society: “the right to a fair trial under established procedures of law.” This hunger for vengeance could not be dismissed as a normal feature of a healthy society. It spoke to an intolerance and bloodlust that was one part Salem, hanging witches on the strength of gossip, and one part frontier, hanging horse-thieves from trees. It was the Puritan spirit, immortalized in Arthur Miller’s play The Crucible, that most troubled Fulbright.

“Although no Western nation has completely dispelled the absolutist spirit of the crusades and the religious wars, some have been more successful than others,” he noted. The core of the democratic idea, going back to the critique of the divine right of kings, was “the element of doubt as to the ability of any man or any movement to perceive ultimate truth.” But “the Puritan way of thinking” injected an absolutist strand into American thought: a ferocious moralism eager to send sinners to hell. Fulbright’s essay recalls much of what the founders wrote about the danger of regression to a psychology of vengeance, and the notion that tyranny exists wherever violence is praised.

Raised on an 18th-century version of the Puritanism that distressed Fulbright, Benjamin Rush had an epiphany one day in 1787, when he chatted with a group of convicts cleaning the streets in Philadelphia. With their shaven heads and degrading uniforms, the men made a sorry spectacle as they begged him for a penny. Offering them a draught of beer instead, Rush was stunned by their humor and humanity as he listened to their stories. The strange thought began to dawn that criminals were humans, after all, and that no heart is “wholly corrupted.” To terminate such a life, or confine it to perpetual misery, was a crime against human nature, Rush wrote. America had won its independence from Britain, but true freedom—freedom from cruelty and arbitrary violence—was still distant, as long as Americans persisted in brutal punishments.

To shed blood with little or no emotion, to treat a criminal like a sheep or a dog, was to demonstrate how little we have understood about liberty as a principle of life and republicanism as its protection. “An execution in a republic,” he argued, “is like a human sacrifice in religion.” It was a return to a world that should have been left behind. 

Rush was not alone. Integral to early American patriotism was the notion of a rational people, liberated from the “bloody code” of medieval law. A critical influence on Rush, Jefferson, and several of their contemporaries was the Italian philosopher Cesare Beccaria, whose Essay on Crimes and Punishments codified this notion of the death penalty as sanctified barbarism. It had taken centuries for societies to evolve from blood feuds and trial by combat to a system of tangible laws, in which the state serves as “the cool moderator of the passions of individuals.”

When the state takes up the sword of vengeance, Beccaria suggests, it forgets its very purpose in life. It falls into the absurdity of trying to prevent murder by committing murder itself. No one could deny that malice and cruelty stalk the gallows. The solemnities of the ritual cannot hide the fact that we are trying to erase a terrible evil with more of the same. And no wonder it fails, observed the Italian. The effect is to cheapen human life and to breed contempt for the law—because it’s hard to love a government that acts in the spirit of “the assassin.”

This was the idea that inspired Jefferson, as he set about reforming Virginia’s penal code, confining capital punishment to murder and treason, and drastically reducing the number of physical punishments on the books. “Let mercy be the character of the law-giver,” he wrote. But let the law be as certain as gravity. Jefferson denied that in disputing “the sanguinary hue of our penal laws” he was being soft on crime or naïvely optimistic about human nature. For laws to be effective, they had to be reasonable, proportionate, and mild. One of his models was William Penn, who showed that the “principles of peace, of reason and right” can hold their own in the realm of government. Although it’s unfortunate that he did not practice what he preached, Jefferson’s remarks on the corrosive effects of slavery reflected his notion that violence is a contagion and the law must limit its spread. “[F]or man is an imitative animal,” he wrote, and imitation is the seed of all education. When the child sees the parent lashing out, he “catches the lineaments of wrath.” Thus “nursed” and trained in tyranny, a tyrant is what he becomes.

Advocates of the death penalty speak of justice, closure, and peace for the victims. But by Jefferson’s lights, a public execution is an education in brutality and a reopening of wounds. The legendary defense lawyer Clarence Darrow argued similarly that to punish murder with death is to “make less serious” the original offense. It is to baptize violence as the way of the world, and to say that what goes around comes around. 

Like Vonnegut, Darrow saw the death penalty as institutionalized vengeance, and he pleaded for an attitude of “mercy” to break the spell. “If our state is not kinder, more human, more considerate, more intelligent than the mad act of these two sick boys,” he said, as he attempted to spare two teenage killers a sentence of death in 1924, “then I’m sorry that I’ve lived so long.” But “I know the future is on my side.” 

Yet Darrow, believed to be the most brilliant and hard-headed attorney of his time, would be dismissed as a snowflake in ours. His language of clemency and kindness would likely be laughed at in an age when a Marine Corps veteran can kill a homeless passenger on the New York subway and walk free of all charges—and even be lauded as a model of civic virtue. 

We all share the disease. President Bill Clinton’s decision to interrupt his presidential campaign to deny clemency for a brain-damaged black man on death row, in 1992, captures the true story of the past 30 years: convergence. “The real Bill Clinton is not for capital punishment,” said Illinois congressman Abner Mikva. He just thought it was “a political necessity.” Mikva saw the same dynamic playing out with handguns, lamenting a shift, in his lifetime, from serious talk of prohibition to the modern politician’s terror of uttering a word against the deadly weapons.

What stems the tide? While Secretary of State Marco Rubio scolds Europe for building “downwards” and sacrificing the greatness of the Western tradition “to the average, the ordinary, the mediocre,” it is worth noting that every European nation except Belarus has abolished capital punishment, and that the nations with whom America shares the practice are those we have been taught to despise for their “cult of death.” We sit behind China, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Yemen among the countries with the highest number of executions per annum. 

My hope is that more states will follow California’s lead in declaring state-sanctioned killing incompatible with “justice and human decency,” as Governor Gavin Newsom wrote last week, when he commuted the sentences of the state’s 548 death row inmates. Although some of the relatives of the victims expressed their fury at Newsom’s decision, one welcomed it in terms that would have pleased Benjamin Rush.

“We used to think that having a vengeful death penalty sentence is going to be what gave us justice,” Jess Nichol, stepsister of Polly Klass, who was murdered in 1993, told The New York Times. “We’ve discovered that it doesn’t.” 

Having at first thought that the killer deserved death, Ms. Nichol came to believe that healing required a degree of mercy. “I want to live in a world where I am well, and not haunted by the hungry ghost of vengeance,” she said. 

This, I would argue, has to be the future.

title: The True Story Behind Get Huge and a Series of Unexplained Deaths Linked to Looksmaxxing
content:
“A day natty is a day wasted.”

That’s the motto of Tony Huge, a prominent figure in the looksmaxxing community. In Huge’s lingo, “natty” means “natural,” as in refraining from using a heavy regimen of supplements popular in the rapidly growing online subculture of men that promotes extreme measures to maximize the potential of one’s physical appearance. Especially popular among young adults and teenagers, looksmaxxing often includes risky behavior like the use of trenbolone, a steroid designed to promote muscle growth in livestock that’s illegal for human use in the United States, and DNP, a toxic fertilizer that can burn fat but brings the potential for deadly side effects. For looksmaxxers, the goal is to achieve peak physical form to become more powerful and attractive to women—life expectancy be damned. 

Filmmaker Stacey Lee first met Huge in late 2024, when looksmaxxing was still “a very fringe movement.” She was embarking on a project about the phenomenon, which she says has moved “to center stage” between then and the Nov. 10 release of her three-part series Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death, streaming on Hulu and Disney+. 

The idea of injecting yourself with dangerous substances to become more muscular, or engaging in bone smashing—repeatedly striking your facial bones with blunt instruments in hopes your bones will heal thicker and stronger—may sound horrifying to most. But Lee understands the appeal. “It begins with a basic human need we all have, no matter our gender, for connection and belonging, and to be seen and respected. I think everyone can relate to the idea that we want to be the best version of ourselves,” she says.

But the goalposts move, and then move again. “You find yourself never being able to feel complete,” she says. You might achieve a buff physique or a bigger jawline, but ”these are superficial solutions to very deep and complex problems.”

Get Huge chronicles the rise of Tony Huge and the growing community of looksmaxxing. Along the way, it appears to brush up against true crime, as Lee delves into a string of unexplained deaths in the community.

The rise of a looksmaxxer

Tony Huge, a former bankruptcy lawyer, founded Enhanced Athlete in 2013 as a brand and YouTube channel. It was there that he first discussed experimenting with anabolic compounds, Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators (SARMs), and other techniques to build muscle. In 2016, he expanded Enhanced Athlete to include a supplement company that also sold unapproved performance-enhancing drugs.. The company was raided by the FDA following the launch of a criminal investigation alleging the manufacturing and distribution of unapproved SARMs and other chemicals. Its CEO, Scott Cavell, was arrested for selling fertilizer as an enhancement and went to prison for three years. Huge, Enhanced Athlete’s co-founder and brand ambassador, was not indicted. He soon moved to Pattaya, Thailand, where the drug laws are considerably more relaxed. 

“Tony has this aura of radical transparency,” says Lee. “But it’s very controlled. He’s got an incredible way of working within gray areas. He’s managed to create a business and lifestyle that allows him to live on the very edge within the realms of the law—at least in Thailand.”

From Pattaya, Huge established a considerable fandom as a looksmaxxer. Though his once-popular YouTube channel has been banned since 2023, he still has nearly 175,000 followers on Instagram. “Tony offered community. He offered a father figure. He offered a blueprint for his life that had never been offered before,” says Lee. His sex life is also central to his appeal. “He’s got anywhere between eight and 10 girlfriends at any point in time, and the house is run by them,” explains Lee. “They make his food, get his supplements ready, do his laundry, and clean his house.”

That combination was enticing to Elon Muskular, one of the subjects Lee interviews in the docuseries. Before coming across Tony, Muskular had been depressed and disconnected. He started messaging Tony to express his admiration, before Tony invited him to move to Thailand, live with him, and run his marketing. Muskular dropped out of school and made the move. “He finds people at rock bottom, who don’t have anything to lose,” Muskular says of Huge in the docuseries. Muskular fell out with Huge over differing views and concerns over Huge’s treatment of other looksmaxxers, and the two no longer work together.

Trouble in paradise

Leo Longevity also counted himself as an admirer of Tony. The self-proclaimed biohacker became well known online for his videos about penis enhancement. In 2022, Leo moved to Thailand to live at Tony’s compound so the two could make videos together as part of the content creation aspect of both of their businesses. Once Huge and Leo got into a groove of creating together, they would publish several videos on YouTube everyday, a nearly unmatchable rate for competitors. The two became incredibly close friends, but the pressure to live up to expectations weighed heavily. 

“In the biohacking/looksmaxxing space, the motivation towards extremes is because you always have to create a new precedent,” says Lee. “Back in the day, Tony was the most controversial guy on the internet, and now he’s looking at what other looksmaxxers would do. He’s like, ‘I got to keep up with this.’” 

It was against this backdrop of immense pressure that tragedy struck. Leo and Huge’s relationship began to feel strained. There was a struggle for power, as both men wanted to be the dominant alpha in their videos, and each had his own ideas about how to achieve those goals. There was also a new protegé in place in Connor Murphy, a rising star on the looksmaxxing scene who joined the duo in Pattaya at the beginning of 2023. The series suggests that Tony was infatuated with Connor, which infuriated Leo. According to Get Huge, on Jan. 27, 2023, Leo began to isolate himself. He was found dead three days later in a bathroom in Huge’s house. 

Leo Longevity’s autopsy report, according to sources close to Pattaya police, indicates that his fatal injuries were caused by another person. The investigation into his death remains open, and no suspect has been identified. Huge has denied any involvement. 

A history of suspicious deaths and disappearances

Get Huge rewinds the story to shed light on another tragic death that took place in Huge’s circle years earlier. Super Beast, Tony’s former chemist, says in the docuseries that Nick Weisser, a close friend of Huge’s and his IT guy, had regular falling-outs with his friend and boss. Super Beast recalls that Weisser attempted to blackmail Huge, threatening to leak critical information about Enhanced, and was found dead a couple of weeks later.

Josh Brooks, a fellow looksmaxxer who Huge describes as a “best friend” in the docuseries, was another of his protegés. Brooks, Super Beast explains in the series, also tried to blackmail Tony, and took his mentor’s business branding and tried to slightly alter it and pass it off as his own. In 2021, there was a fire in Brooks' apartment in Colombia, and he fell out of the window to his death. 

In 2022, Coach Trevor, another of Huge’s close friends, disappeared. “I personally don’t know what happened to him. None of us do,” Super Beast remarks in Get Huge. In 2024, Scott Cavell, the CEO of Enhanced Athlete, was found dead in a hotel. An official cause of death hasn’t been released, though Super Beast says he believes that Cavell was killed. “Scott did drugs. He wouldn’t do the amount that killed him,” he says. He does stop short of making accusations for who is responsible for any of these deaths and disappearances. (Huge has not been declared a suspect.) But he has plenty to say about Huge’s empire: “It’s not a brotherhood. It’s a gathering point for weak-minded people. They don’t take care of each other. They don’t uplift each other. They find ways to f-ck each other’s lives up. Basically a cyclone.”

Filming for Get Huge wrapped in June of 2026—until a new development brought the team back into production. On July 7, Connor Murphy died by drowning in the lake in his backyard in Thailand. He had been exhibiting increasingly erratic behavior, including claiming that he was gaining superpowers after injecting gold into his bloodstream. As of the docuseries’ release, Murphy’s death is believed to be an accident. 

How far can looksmaxxing go?

While Get Huge investigates the deaths of Leo Longevity and others connected to Tony Huge, it’s also a broader look at the rise of the looksmaxxing movement itself. In one scene, Huge travels to Las Vegas for a bodybuilding show, where he meets a group of teens as young as 13. Concerned with the decrease in brand awareness as younger looksmaxxers like Clavicular and Androgenic increase their share of the fandom, he appears to be looking to increase his reach to younger audiences. “Tony doesn’t have the same gravitas with the next generation, and that leads him to Vegas to try and figure out how to capture a piece of that pie,” says Lee. Just moments into their conversation, one of them asks if Huge can get them steroids. He laughs off the question, but it lingers.

“The challenge of this experimental biohacking culture,” says Lee, “is that our bodies are all very different. One thing that works for Tony Huge might not work for the 16-year-old kid in Iowa who just wants to get jacked.” There’s also no need for any of these looksmaxxers to verify that they’re actually taking what they’re claiming. Clavicular, currently the most popular looksmaxxer, says he does meth to help maintain his physique. “He may not be taking what he’s saying he’s taking, and this kid who’s using it as a blueprint for his life doesn’t have the discernment to know that,” Lee says.

Safeguards implemented by social media platforms, including Huge’s YouTube ban, have played a role in his decreasing reach. But he and other looksmaxxers decry these removals as censorship. And Lee understands that anything that’s perceived as censorship “can get weaponized,” using Andrew Tate as an example. “Every time he gets censored, he uses it as part of his argument, and it galvanizes more followers,” says Lee. “If they get kicked off YouTube, they go to Rumble, they go to 4Chan. Whatever the most underground forum is.”

Lee holds out some hope that the rise of looksmaxxing might be curbed. “I think what we’re witnessing now is a dismantling of these power structures of masculinity and more of a reckoning. The Tate brothers are on trial, and you’re seeing a turning of the tide politically.” 

What does concern Lee is the rising use of AI in looksmaxxing. Her series shows that Tony’s team regularly produces and creates content using AI. “Even if Tony’s not around, he can live forever on the internet using those tools,” she says.

Adds Lee: “If the humans stop, do the machines carry it on?”

title: The 10 Best Gifts for Health and Fitness Nuts
content:
Every year, TIME's editors and correspondents work together to compile a collection of the most interesting and groundbreaking new products and innovations for the Best Inventions list. As holiday season approaches, the TIME team has pulled out a selection of the 10 best health and fitness items from the list that would make a perfect gift for the most sporty people in your life.

Speediance Gym Nano

Portable weight training

Gym Nano is a portable digital resistance engine that can latch onto most racks, with a 16.7 ft. cable and a weight range of 7.7- to 220-lb. It also has sensors to capture athlete data and performance progression. —TIME Staff

Buy Now: Gym Nano on Speediance

Form Smart Swim 2 Pro

Goggles that coach

Because you can’t hear underwater or check your watch while swimming laps, accessing real-time metrics has been nearly impossible. Now, Form’s augmented reality goggles not only project split times onto their patented glass but also guide athletes through personalized pool workouts and offer technique coaching right in their field of vision. The ergonomic goggles also come with open-water navigation built in, a feature inspired by triathletes who, according to Form founder and CEO Dan Eisenhardt, “complained they had a hard time in races going straight between two points.” And yes, you can also upload your workouts to Strava. —Matthew Huff

Buy Now: Form Smart Swim 2 Pro on Amazon

MyCelsius Cooling Bracelet

Instant relief for hot flashes

While treatments for perimenopause and menopause symptoms have gotten more sophisticated, sometimes you just need immediate relief from hot flashes. The MyCelsius Cooling Bracelet sends a cold sensation to the wearer’s wrist, a thermally sensitive area, with the push of a button. But there’s no cooling agent involved; instead, its patent-pending miniature thermoelectric system actively pulls heat away from the skin. The device, now sold in Europe and headed for the U.S. next year, also has a Night Mode for gentler, periodic cooling. “It's almost like a switch to tell the brain, ‘You do not need to sweat all of this heat out,’” says cofounder and CEO Maxime Kryvian. —Eliza Thompson

Buy Now: MyCelsius Cooling Bracelet on MyCelsius

GoRuck Spy Ruck

A weighted vest for women 

Rucking—or walking while wearing a weighted backpack or vest—is all the rage, with weighted vest sales surging more than 50% to $27 million in the year ending May 2025. But many rucks are bulky and designed with men’s flatter chests in mind. “Our bodies are more complicated,” says GoRuck founder and former CIA case officer Emily McCarthy, who devised a solution with the Spy Ruck. The weights sit on the back and sides, meaning the front part of the chest stays unencumbered while the wearer gets her workout in. The low-profile design is not nearly as unwieldy as a traditional ruck, so women on-the-go can build muscle while running errands. —Eliza Thompson

Buy Now: GoRuck Spy Ruck on Amazon

Nike ACG Radical Airflow Shirt

A cooling running top

Nike’s “All Conditions Gear” label has historically been focused on casual hiking. But when Beaverton began conceptualizing a relaunch of the line in 2024, the designers shifted their focus to the growing sport of trail running, where marquee races are rarely shorter than 50km. At last year’s Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run, Nike equipped ACG athlete Caleb Olson with the Radical Airflow Shirt, a loose-fitting long sleeve pocked with hundreds of large holes. Each of these perforations is shaped like a funnel, leveraging the Venturi effect to suck cooling air to the skin as you run. Despite sweltering conditions, Olson not only managed to win the race, but was only two minutes off the course record. The shirt is now available to the public. —Daniel Varghese

Buy now: Nike ACG Radical Airflow NXT at nike

Laced Golf Gen 1 Alignment System

Sensors that fix your alignment

In an era where golfers can adjust their game with a wide array of tech-forward gadgets, it’s mind-boggling that alignment is still best corrected using simple wooden sticks. Which is why golf buddies Tyler Kenney and Zach Smith founded Laced Golf, a digital device that clips onto your shoelaces and gives you real-time feedback on your stance using lights and haptic vibration. When the light turns green, swing—and hopefully hit your shot with more accuracy than ever. Tourney Mode, meanwhile, records movement silently so competitive golfers can review data after a game. “It uncovers blind spots for almost everyone we test with,” says Kenney. —Eliza Thompson

Buy Now: Gen 1 Alignment System on Laced Golf

Hypershell X Ultra S

Smooth-moving exoskeleton

The global exoskeleton market is poised to reach $1.79 billion by 2033, so it’s safe to say robotic wearables are in demand. But if there’s a common complaint, it’s that they can feel rigid. Hypershell X Ultra S addresses that with its HyperIntuition algorithm, which analyzes and anticipates a user's movements in real time, allowing for more fluid motion. “It’s similar to end-to-end driving systems in autonomous cars, mapping human motion directly into assistive movement,” says Toby Knisely, Director of Global Communications. Whether you're running, hiking, or cycling, the all-terrain Hypershell can offset up to 86 pounds of weight, adding an almost literal spring to your step. —Matthew Huff

Buy Now: Hypershell X Ultra S on Amazon

Swift Hockey ZT Pro 2

Making pro-quality sticks more accessible

The high cost of ice hockey gear can be a barrier to entry for players—particularly composite sticks, which can cost around $400 and may break after just a few months of play. Former minor-league player Zechariah Thomas founded Swift Hockey in 2022 at age 19, with the goal of delivering pro-quality sticks for less via a primarily direct-to-consumer business model. This year, the company released the ZT Pro 2, a second-generation of its flagship stick: priced at up to $199.99, its shaft features unique rounded edges for easier handling, and added layers of carbon in both its core and blade for extra durability. Players at the highest level now use Swift sticks, including 2026 NHL draft pick Landon Halfele and multiple players in the Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) and the NCAA. —Avery Stone

Buy Now: Swift Hockey ZT Pro 2 on Swift

Garmin Cirqa

No screen, no subscription, just fitness

Whoop and Oura Ring helped popularize screenless wearables, but they also normalized paywalled health insights. Garmin’s new Cirqa smart band changes that. “We’re giving you your insights without having to lock you into additional prices” says Jill Kaiser, Cirqa product manager. The Cirqa looks nearly identical to a Whoop and addresses one of the category's biggest frustrations: unreliable automatic workout detection. A dedicated side button lets people manually start and stop their most popular activity without their phone, giving them the freedom to run, lift, or play ball without distractions. —Hannah Singleton

Buy Now: Garmin Cirqa on Amazon

Reebok Smart Eyewear Powered by Lucyd

Audio sunglasses for athletes

There’s so much gear associated with working out—fitness trackers, watches, headphones, sunglasses. Reebok is lightening that load by combining two into one. Made in partnership with smart eyewear company Lucyd, the Reebok Powered by Lucyd sunglasses let you play music, listen to podcasts, take phone calls, or receive voice instructions, all through the sport sunglasses’ arms, without tuning out the world around you. Available in six styles—two of which are prescription-ready—each pair features polarized lenses, lightweight frames, noise-cancelling microphones, and open-ear hi-fi audio. —Matt Alderton

Buy Now: Reebok Smart Eyewear on Amazon

title: How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate
content:
The dark web isn't just for illicit activities. In fact, many legitimate online platforms maintain a ".onion" domain on the dark web for privacy reasons, including media outlets like ProPublica and BBC News, social media sites like Facebook, and privacy-conscious communication platforms like Proton Mail and SecureDrop. 

But this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious users. And given that onion links are long and jumbled, it’s easy for users to accidentally click on the wrong link and end up on a fake website instead of the real one. When the FBI seized 276 onion addresses during 2014's Operation Onymous, they found that 153 of them were phishing sites.

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for. 

How phishing works on the dark web

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish. 

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones. 

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security. 

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015. 

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source. 

How to verify an onion site in Tor Browser

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website. 

  1. The Tor Project has a feature called Onion-Location, which lets clear web websites advertise that they have a dark web version available for users who prefer more privacy. If opening a regular TLS-backed website using the Tor Browser reveals a purple “onion available” button in the address bar, you can click on it and be redirected to the official onion link associated with that site. 

  2. On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

  3. When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to. 

  4. On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

  5. Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit. 

What to do if you think you've been phished

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged. 

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

title: 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know
content:
As streaming platforms go, Hulu has a lot to offer, with curated TV shows and movies as well as live TV. Hulu is also fairly flexible when it comes to curating separate profiles, watching across multiple devices, and accessing content while traveling. If you're a Hulu subscriber, these are the best hacks to maximize your streaming experience.

Curate your Hulu watch history to avoid cluttered suggestions

If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Add a PIN to your profile to prevent other viewers from influencing your algorithm

If PIN protection is enabled, users must enter a four-digit PIN when switching between profiles on a single account. This is intended as a parental control feature, since it's available on non-Kids profiles and can keep children from accessing more mature content on an adult's profile. However, you can also enable this feature to keep other users from seeing your viewing history and preferences or influencing your algorithm by watching their content under your profile (accidentally or on purpose). To set up a PIN, log into your account on Hulu's website, select your profile, and go to Manage Profiles > Parental Controls. You'll have to choose a PIN and enter your password to confirm the changes.

Create a dedicated guest or watch party profile to keep your profile private

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

Change your subtitle settings to manage how they appear on your screen

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

Pause your subscription instead of canceling while you travel or wait for new content

If you won't be using your Hulu account for several weeks or months but don't want to cancel your account entirely, you can pause billing so you're not paying for time you're not watching. This is a good option if you have extended travel planned or are waiting for new seasons of specific shows to drop. Pauses can last up to 12 weeks for monthly subscribers. Note that if you do cancel Hulu, you can simply resubscribe to regain access to your profile. You can request a pause and set the duration under Account > Your Subscription > Pause Your Subscription.

Use the expiring content badge to prioritize your watch list

If you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

Transfer your profile to keep what you’ve curated when switching to a new account

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

Use Manage Devices to remove your account from hotel, Airbnb, or friends’ TVs

If you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Manage download resolution for offline viewing to save space on your device

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

Log into Hulu on home wifi to prevent losing access to live TV while on the road

If you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

title: 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know
content:
If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Hide your post history to keep your profile private

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Use Old Reddit by default to disable infinite scrolling

Credit: Pranay Parab

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access

Turn off annoying subreddit styles to make reading easier

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Disable social features to stop strangers from bothering you

Reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Create multireddits to follow your favorite hobbies

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Turn off ad personalization and block ads to reduce tracking

If you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Disable all email alerts to stop Reddit's spammy messages

Credit: Pranay Parab

Reddit's notifications are spammy enough that I have no desire to get a copy of those alerts via email. You can easily disable all of Reddit's email alerts by going to Reddit Settings > Email, and enabling Unsubscribe from all emails.

Bypass Reddit's new feeds to sort posts in your preferred order

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Use a throwaway email ID to create burner accounts on Reddit

Reddit doesn't let you sign up without an email address or phone number anymore. This makes it a little annoying to create burner accounts, but it's not impossible. In fact, you can create multiple Reddit accounts with the same email address, as long as you use aliases on Gmail or any other email service of your choice. For more privacy, you can use services that provide disposable email addresses, such as Yopmail.

Use advanced search filters to search Reddit like a pro

After all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

title: The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected
content:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.

The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy. 

Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm)
$389.99 at Amazon
$389.99 at Amazon

I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase. 

What are Siri Recaps, and where do they fit among the other Audio Intelligence features? 

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":

  • Music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

  • Sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature. 

  • Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

  • Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there? 

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just said in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all. 

How to turn on Siri recaps

At least for now, the feature is only available in a developer beta, so sign up for that now if you want to try it. You'll need an Apple Watch Series 12 (or Ultra 4) and an iPhone 16 or better, excluding the 16e. (I have a 16 Pro, so I'm good.)

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

What I found in my Siri recaps

As promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was said. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct. 

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people said to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.)

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough. 

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful. 

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

Siri recaps may be useful, but at what cost? 

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded. 

But it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it. 

I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most important points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch. 

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.
